reviews.reason: The allowed real-analysis tools do not identify arithmetic structure from an abstract ternary relation. The proof must recover small scales through iterated nontriangle witnesses, force continuity from triangles, prevent switching the two complementary intervals, recover addition, and then obtain a common scale without assuming rational closure of the distance set. These are linked, nonroutine rigidity obligations.
reviews.core_assessment: Read complete proof1023-1054 and the previously read definitions394-400,566-571,891-897. The decreasing delta_i sequence also decreases geometrically after f; it supplies uniform continuity away from0. On a closed bounded subinterval, uniform continuity and density give the finite chain used in1041, so each complementary source interval has a single target side. The small delta_i images select the lower side, and bijectivity forces the complementary equalities. Interior additivity then follows by continuity, and the rational-approximation argument only uses positive integer multiples that remain below the supremum, hence in the distance value set. No assumption of rational divisibility is made.
reviews.prerequisite_assessment: Only elementary real analysis and the explicit distance-set/triangle definitions are used. Density follows from positive arbitrarily small elements and closure under capped sums; this is routine and does not replace the rigidity argument.

proof_completeness.reason: All substantive steps appear in the original proof. The attained finite-supremum case follows by the already established continuity, approximating one summand from below in the dense distance set; its sums remain in the set by capped-addition closure. This is a boundary instance of the author limit method, not an independently invented missing core.

standard_prerequisites.statement: Uniform continuity on intervals, density, rational approximation and limits.
standard_prerequisites.use: Convert triangle constraints into continuity and then constant ratios; none of the rigidity conclusions is assumed.

core_obligations: Recover a null sequence in the target from a rapidly decreasing source sequence using only the ternary triangle relation.
Use triangles with one small side to prove uniform continuity away from zero.
Separate the two components outside each triangle interval and recover additivity from their boundary behavior.
Use rational approximation from below and truncated-addition closure to prove a common positive scale factor, without assuming division closure of the distance set.

proof_roadmap.step: Derive density and a rapidly decreasing image null sequence, then continuity/uniform continuity away from zero.
Recover triangle-interval complements, rule out mixing their two sides by small-step chains, and identify the additive boundary.
Approximate t/x by rationals and x/m from below within the distance set; use continuity and existing finite sums to get f(t)/t=f(x)/x.

approved_task_config.difficulty_reason: A bare triangle-preserving bijection need not be assumed monotone or continuous. The proof reconstructs these analytic constraints from the relational structure, then obtains additivity and a single scale factor even when the domain is only a countable truncated additive set and is not closed under division. The null-sequence and rational-approximation arguments solve those specific obstructions.

compared.difference: The public item assumes inf=1 and unbounded sup, and gets equality of normalized sets. Here inf=0, including bounded sets, and every triangle-isomorphism is multiplication by one positive real.
The other new task constructs nonrigid bounded sets with positive infimum that code arbitrary order isomorphism; this is the opposite accumulating-at-zero rigidity theorem.
Rado spanning-subgraph equivalence for a nontrivial neighbourhood filter; no triangle-isomorphism coding or scalar rigidity.
Back-and-forth ranks for ordinal powers of integer orders, not triangle equivalence of distance value sets.
Integral separating vector under a triangular matrix action, not coding or rigidity of metric triangles.
Two bounded-component Borel covers obtained from a forward-independent hitting set, not metric triangle equivalence.
